result.summary: This PR migrates the CoinGrinder coin-selection unit tests from the older coinselector_tests.cpp file into the newer coinselection_tests.cpp suite, which uses effective values and real feerates instead of ad-hoc parameters. It also simplifies the exhaustion test to use only two distinct UTXO weights instead of many, and tidies a few shared test helpers (MakeCoin, HaveEquivalentInputs). Each commit migrates one test case to ease review. The old duplicated test file is reduced by 253 lines with 194 lines of the tests re-added in the new location.
result.problem: The project has two coin-selection test files, coinselector_tests.cpp and coinselection_tests.cpp, and the CoinGrinder coverage lives in the older, less realistic one; this creates duplicated test infrastructure and inconsistency for wallet test maintainers, as yancyribbens notes: 'It would be nice to see the coinselector test file removed entirely in the future since having multiple test files has caused confusion.'

open_concerns: l0rinc suggested simplifying HaveEquivalentInputs further and dropping the now-redundant is_eff_value parameter and expected_amount assertion.

l0rinc suggested restructuring scenarios into independently runnable named Boost test cases with shared macros, referencing headers_sync_chainwork_tests.cpp as a model, and has already implemented many of these suggestions in a separate branch.
yancyribbens flagged odd magic numbers (max_selection_weight of 40000 vs 400000) as possibly a pre-existing typo, unrelated to this PR.
Author has stated there are still minor things to tweak before this is finalized.

result.card: This PR migrates CoinGrinder coin-selection unit tests from the older coinselector_tests.cpp into the newer, more realistic coinselection_tests.cpp suite, and slightly simplifies the exhaustion test. It is a pure test-infrastructure change with no effect on wallet behavior or fund safety; its value is tidiness and eventual retirement of a duplicated test file, which yancyribbens explicitly wants ('having multiple test files has caused confusion'). Both commenting reviewers gave Concept ACK with no objections, but l0rinc has proposed a substantial alternative restructuring (implemented in a separate branch) that the author may fold in, and the author has said there are still tweaks planned. Because of this likely rework and a currently failing (reportedly unrelated) CI run, the PR is Paused rather than ready for a full line-by-line review. No dependencies block it and it blocks nothing else of note.
